gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states which replacement switches the roughly $37 Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 takes (TechXReviews: other 3-pin magnetic switches such as Gateron or TTC), or that its qmk.top web driver has no polling-rate selector.
standout_why: I read mechanicalkeyboard.net (rank 1), setupinsider.com (rank 3) and gamepadsquire.com (rank 5/9). None lists the NS68, so none has its switch or driver facts. But gamepadsquire already states the wired-versus-2.4 GHz polling split for the AULA F75 HE (8,000 Hz wired, 1,000 Hz on 2.4 GHz) and the MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra TMR (8,000 Hz on both), so the idea is not new to the result set. The two cited pages (PC Gamer's Hall effect guide, which names the NS68, and RTINGS' rapid trigger research) returned only navigation text, so I could not check whether they already carry it. The cell that would lift this to a 2 or 3, Gamakay's own statement of polling rate per connection mode and of switch polarity for the NS68 Wired and Tri-mode variants, could not be opened: gamakay.com returned HTTP 429 on all seven attempts.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. Every budget board named in the pages I read is rated 8,000 Hz over USB, and on the one tri-mode board whose 2.4 GHz rate they give in this price band (AULA F75 HE) it falls to 1,000 Hz. So a shopper who wants rapid trigger at full polling plugs in the cable either way, and paying extra for wireless buys convenience, not speed. On that basis the NS68 Wired ($36.79 in the partner table you supplied, read 2026-11-21) sits level on connection with the wired-only MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro, Redragon K617 HE and Epomaker HE68 Lite, and adds arrow keys as a 65% board. The NS68 Tri-mode ($39.99 in the same table) would be the low-cost wireless option, but its wireless polling rate must be read from Gamakay's page before the page prints it.
